llm.summary: The skill claims a Python-based Moodle client and MCP server, but the bundle contains only documentation and a package.json; it instructs cloning and running external code (and using environment secrets) that are not declared in the skill metadata — this mismatch warrants caution.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md describes multiple Python programs (moodle_connector.py, batch_downloader.py, mcp_server.py) and a full feature set, but the skill bundle contains no Python code — only SKILL.md and package.json. That mismatch (documentation without implementation) is incoherent: a consumer following the skill would need to fetch and execute an external repository to get the claimed capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the user/agent to git clone a GitHub repo, pip install requirements, run Python scripts, and add an MCP server entry that supplies MOODLE_CRED_PASSWORD via env. Those steps involve network fetches and execution of external code not included in the skill; they also instruct handling of secrets (Moodle tokens, encryption password) even though the skill metadata declared no required env vars or credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the registry entry, but package.json contains an install script that runs 'pip install -r requirements.txt' and 'playwright install chromium'. The SKILL.md instructs cloning from GitHub and running pip. Fetching and executing code from an external GitHub repo and installing Playwright (which downloads browsers) are moderate-to-high risk actions when done automatically or without audit.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill metadata lists no required env vars, yet SKILL.md expects users to set MOODLE_CRED_PASSWORD and to place web_service_token in config.json. Asking for an encryption password and a Moodle token is reasonable for a Moodle connector, but the omission from declared requires.env is an inconsistency that reduces transparency. The skill also instructs storing tokens in a local config file (with advice not to commit) — this is expected but sensitive.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default autonomous invocation are normal. The SKILL.md suggests the user add an MCP server entry to their Claude Code config (a user action that modifies a local app config) — this is not automatic in the bundle but does increase persistent integration surface if the user follows it. No evidence the skill requests system-wide privileges beyond this.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or run this skill blindly. Key concerns: (1) the package lacks any Python source files described in the docs — the SKILL.md expects you to git clone and run an external repo; (2) following the instructions will install and execute third-party code and download browsers (Playwright), which can access files and network; (3) secrets (Moodle token, MOODLE_CRED_PASSWORD) are required by the runtime but aren't declared in the skill metadata; (4) the README/license text is inconsistent (mentions both MIT and GPLv3). Recommended next steps: inspect the referenced GitHub repository (https://github.com/Jabir-Srj/moodle-connector) before running anything; review the actual Python source, requirements.txt, and mcp_server.py for unexpected network endpoints, telemetry, or credential exfiltration; prefer running in a sandboxed VM or container; use least-privilege tokens for Moodle and don't reuse high-privilege credentials; verify author identity and recent commits; if you want the skill in an automated agent, require the distributor to include the actual vetted code in the skill bundle or provide a signed release you can audit. If you cannot audit the upstream code, treat this skill as untrusted.
